label: Federated tenant posture
query: What should Lakeshore L0 see that Morgan Street L1 should not automatically see at transaction grain?
answer: At transaction grain, I’d draw a hard line between “enterprise control / risk” vs “operating-unit execution.” L0 at Lakeshore sits on the former; Morgan Street L1 is the latter. My read: Lakeshore L0 should see by default at transaction grain: 1) Cross-entity exposure and control – All-bank cash movements and intraday positions (e.g., Kyriba-level visibility across Morgan Street plus other banners / entities). – Intercompany settlements and upstream/downstream funding flows across subsidiaries. – Counterparty/concentration views: exposure to a single bank, broker, or large customer/supplier cutting across Morgan Street. 2) Sensitive governance attributes – Mandates, signatory limits, and approval breaks tied to named executives and governance bodies. – Exceptions/overrides flags: transactions pushed through outside standard policy, sanctions-screen hits, AML / fraud alerts. 3) True cost-of-funds and transfer pricing – Internal transfer-pricing rates, liquidity charges, and treasury allocation mechanics at deal/transaction level. – Funding source tags (holdco revolver vs local facility vs internal note). Morgan Street L1 should not automatically see at transaction grain: 1) Cross-entity and peer visibility – No line-of-sight to other Lakeshore subsidiaries’ transactions, positions, or counterparty deals by default. – No ability to reconstruct Lakeshore-wide liquidity or hedging posture from Morgan Street. 2) Governance / surveillance detail – No access to enterprise-wide exception logs, sanctions hits across entities, or group fraud investigations. – Limited view of approval hierarchy beyond “approved / rejected” for their own cost centers.
